dedupe_keys.name: changes in anthropogenic influences on us streams and rivers over 40 years 16 data themes usgs

description: This USGS data release gives consistent time series of 16 human influences on stream and river water quality for all 15,458 HUC-10 watersheds of the conterminous United States, with land use and imperviousness also for ecoregions and counties, so that change can be tracked over about 40 years. Themes include dams and reservoirs (1972-2013), irrigation, freshwater withdrawals (1985-2010), wastewater treatment plant nitrogen and phosphorus yields (1978-2012), imperviousness, land use, population and housing density, fertiliser, manure, pesticides, road salt, atmospheric deposition and timber cutting. James Falcone of the US Geological Survey's National Water Quality Project produced it and published it on ScienceBase in 2018 as zipped tables and shapefiles, one per theme, as a free public-domain download. Coverage is national; the HUC-10 values can be aggregated to larger hydrologic units. Caveats: source data resolutions range from annual to decadal and end around 2012 to 2014. Simulation uses: watershed-level trends in dams, wastewater loads, irrigation and imperviousness for hazard exposure, capacity planning and climate adaptation studies. Related records: USGS dam impact metrics (data-usgs-dam-impact-disturbance-metrics-conus) and USGS irrigation water use by HUC12 (data-usgs-monthly-irrigation-water-use-huc12-2015).
name: Changes in anthropogenic influences on US streams and rivers over 40 years, 16 data themes (USGS)
notes: Public-domain licence assumed from USGS data release policy; the licence line was not read. File formats inside the zips (tables and shapefiles) are as the description states; CSV and XLSX are inferred from the file list.
provider: US Geological Survey, National Water Quality Project (J. A. Falcone)
